title: Creamy Steak Pasta
summary: Seared beef and tagliatelle in an indulgent Boursin sauce. Comfort food, elegant enough for guests.

steps.text: Mix the cheese with the garlic, parsley, thyme (if using), salt and pepper. Set aside at room temperature.
Pat the steak completely dry and season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat and add the oil. Sear the steak whole for {timer:2-3} per side, until well browned and cooked to your liking. Move it to a plate, rest for {timer:5}, then slice into strips. Lower the heat to medium.
Cook the pasta in boiling salted water until al dente. Do not drain it.
Add the onion to the steak pan and fry for {timer:3-4}, until soft and golden.
Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer. Stir in the cheese mixture until melted, then add the Parmesan, parsley and the steak's resting juices. Simmer gently.
Lift the pasta into the pan with tongs, bringing some of its cooking water with it. Toss vigorously until the sauce clings, adding more water for a silky consistency.
Add the steak strips and toss gently. Finish with Parmesan and parsley and serve straight away.

tips: Cream cheese or mascarpone are good substitutes for Boursin. Do not overcrowd the pan when searing: meat tastes better when it is well seared. Lift the pasta straight into the sauce with tongs; the pasta water binds everything together.
